summary.title: Deep-Learning-based Millimeter-Wave Massive MIMO for Hybrid Precoding
summary.authors: Hongji Huang, Yiwei Song, Jie Yang, Guan Gui, and Fumiyuki Adachi
summary.executive_summary: This paper addresses the high computational complexity and suboptimal performance of existing hybrid precoding schemes in millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive MIMO systems. Traditional methods, such as those based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) or Geometric Mean Decomposition (GMD), struggle to fully exploit the spatial information and sparsity statistics inherent in mmWave channels. To overcome these limitations, the authors propose a deep-learning-enabled framework that treats the hybrid precoder selection as a mapping relation within a Deep Neural Network (DNN). The DNN is structured as an autoencoder, where the input layer captures features, hidden layers perform encoding and noise mixing, and the output layer generates the optimized precoder under power constraints. The training process utilizes an unsupervised learning approach with Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with momentum to minimize the Frobenius norm loss between the target precoder and the DNN output. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DNN-based scheme significantly outperforms conventional SVD-based, GMD-based, and spatially sparse precoding methods in terms of Bit Error Ratio (BER) and spectrum efficiency. Furthermore, the proposed method achieves a lower computational complexity of O(L^2 N_s N_t^2) compared to existing schemes. The study also investigates the impact of hyperparameters such as batch size and learning rate, finding that smaller batch sizes and lower learning rates generally yield better performance, albeit with slower convergence. The work concludes that deep learning effectively solves the non-convex optimization problems in hybrid precoding, offering a promising path for future 5G and beyond communications.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper addresses the high computational complexity and suboptimal performance of existing hybrid precoding schemes in millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive MIMO systems. Traditional methods, such as those based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) or Geometric Mean Decomposition (GMD), struggle to fully exploit the spatial information and sparsity statistics inherent in mmWave channels. To overcome these limitations, the authors propose a deep-learning-enabled framework that treats the hybrid precoder selection as a mapping relation within a Deep Neural Network (DNN). The DNN is structured as an autoencoder, where the input layer captures features, hidden layers perform encoding and noise mixing, and the output layer generates the optimized precoder under power constraints. The training process utilizes an unsupervised learning approach with Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with momentum to minimize the Frobenius norm loss between the target precoder and the DNN output. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DNN-based scheme significantly outperforms conventional SVD-based, GMD-based, and spatially sparse precoding methods in terms of Bit Error Ratio (BER) and spectrum efficiency. Furthermore, the proposed method achieves a lower computational complexity of O(L^2 N_s N_t^2) compared to existing schemes. The study also investigates the impact of hyperparameters such as batch size and learning rate, finding that smaller batch sizes and lower learning rates generally yield better performance, albeit with slower convergence. The work concludes that deep learning effectively solves the non-convex optimization problems in hybrid precoding, offering a promising path for future 5G and beyond communications.

Research Context
Wireless data traffic is predicted to increase by over 10,000-fold by 2030. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands are attractive for 5G due to under-utilized spectrum. Existing hybrid precoding schemes suffer from high computational complexity. Traditional methods like SVD fail to fully exploit spatial information. GMD-based schemes avoid bit allocation but face non-convex constraints. Deep learning is an emerging solution for complex nonlinear problems. Previous works using deep learning in communications include beam selection.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study investigates a framework integrating deep learning into hybrid precoding. The primary hypothesis is that DNNs can capture structural information of hybrid precoding. The DNN is regarded as an autoencoder to optimize multiple layers. The goal is to lower computational complexity while enhancing performance. The method aims to minimize Bit Error Ratio (BER). The approach is expected to enhance spectrum efficiency. The DNN is treated as a black box for mapping relations.

Methodological Details
The system model considers a Base Station (BS) with a Uniform Linear Array (ULA). The BS has Nt antennas and the user has Nr received antennas. The channel model is based on the Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) model. The channel matrix H is defined with P non-line-of-sight components. The carrier frequency is set to 28 GHz in simulations. The number of non-line-of-sight components P is set to 3. The DNN framework is constructed using the Keras library. The input layer is a fully connected layer with 128 units. The first hidden layer comprises 400 units for encoding. The second hidden layer comprises 256 units. A noise layer with 200 units mixes distortion. The third hidden layer has 128 units for decoding. The fourth hidden layer has 64 units. The ReLU function is used as the activation function. A special activation function enforces the power constraint in the output layer. The network was trained for 45,000 iterations. The learning rate is set to 0.001 for robustness analysis.

Procedures And Architectures
The DNN architecture consists of input, hidden, noise, and output layers. The GMD method is used to decompose the channel matrix. The loss function is defined as the Frobenius norm of the difference. The training process is an unsupervised learning approach. Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with momentum is employed. The momentum parameter alpha and learning rate epsilon are used. The algorithm initializes RA and RD as empty matrices. Random data sequences are generated in the DNN for training. The physical AoA and AoD are generated randomly. The DNN is trained until the error threshold is met. The optimal precoders are obtained without requiring iterations after training.

Key Results
The DNN-based method outperforms conventional schemes in BER. The performance improvement is more apparent at higher SNRs. The proposed scheme achieves better spectrum efficiency than others. The computational complexity of the proposed method is O(L^2 N_s N_t^2). The SIC-based scheme has complexity O(2NrNs(Nt^2(K+NsNr))). The spatially sparse method has higher complexity than the proposed one. Performance degrades with increasing batch size in terms of BER. Smaller batch sizes lead to unstable convergence. Lower learning rates optimize hybrid precoding performance. Larger learning rates cause higher validation error. The proposed scheme converges at around 11 iterations. The analog precoding scheme requires about 22 iterations. The MSE performance of the DNN scheme is superior.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Deep learning captures the structural information of the hybrid precoding scheme. The DNN acts as a black box to capture useful features. The method leverages the sparsity statistics of mmWave channels. Deep learning solves non-convex optimization problems in hybrid precoding. The approach reduces hardware complexity and energy consumption. The DNN facilitates hybrid precoding through recognition and mapping abilities.

Contradictions And Limitations
Slower convergence may be induced by a larger batch size. Too small a batch size leads to unstable convergence. Slower convergence behavior is induced by using a lower learning rate. Selecting the best learning rate remains an open issue. The study assumes no information on all communication links. The results are based on simulations, not experimental validation.

Claims
The proposed DNN-based hybrid precoding scheme outperforms conventional SVD and GMD-based methods in BER and spectrum efficiency. The DNN-based method outperforms conventional schemes. The proposed scheme achieves better spectrum efficiency. The performance gap becomes larger as SNR increases. Performance degrades with increasing batch size. Lower learning rates cause slower convergence. Deep learning is effective for mmWave massive MIMO. The method reduces computational complexity.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study investigates the impact of batch size on BER. The study investigates the impact of learning rate on BER. The MSE versus iterations is analyzed for robustness. The proposed scheme converges faster than analog precoding.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the DNN architecture in the proposed scheme. Figure 2 shows BER versus SNR for various schemes. Figure 3 shows BER versus SNR with different batch sizes. Figure 4 shows BER performance with various learning rates. Figure 5 shows spectrum efficiency versus SNR. Figure 6 shows MSE versus iterations. Table I compares the computational complexity of several schemes.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a DNN-based framework for hybrid precoding in mmWave massive MIMO. 2. The strongest evidence is the superior BER and spectrum efficiency compared to SVD and GMD methods. 3. The future path involves applying deep learning to channel feedback issues.
